# Stacklit

> Stacklit writes a small, committable JSON index of a codebase (modules, exports, dependency edges, hints) and a symbol graph, so AI coding agents can orient themselves without re-exploring the repo each session. Free, MIT licensed, one Go binary, deterministic, runs locally with no LLM, and the CLI makes no network calls.

Key facts:
- Install: `npx stacklit init`, `brew install glincker/tap/stacklit`, `npm install -g stacklit`, or `go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest`.
- Output: `stacklit.json` (index), a Mermaid dependency file (`DEPENDENCIES.md` by default, `output.mermaid` in `.stacklitrc.json`), `stacklit.html` (interactive map), `stacklit derive` (compact text map for prompts).
- Deterministic: same repo gives the same bytes. Hard token budgets on queries (`--budget`).
- Languages: 48 languages and formats in the index; the symbol graph (query, explain, impact, path, hubs, slice) covers 20 languages.
- Assistants: `stacklit setup` configures 26 targets, including Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Cline, Zed and a generic AGENTS.md. MCP server via `stacklit serve` (stdio, 15 tools, or `--profile minimal` for 4).
- Privacy: no telemetry, no account, no upload. The generated HTML map requests small language logos from thesvg.org unless `STACKLIT_MAP_ICONS=off`. The only opt-in external call is `stacklit init --summary`.
- Benchmarks: reproducible, no LLM calls, six pinned repos. The derived map is 137 to 1,351 tokens. The benchmark does not show a token saving over grep; it shows cheap orientation. Limitations are documented.
- Agent test: two rounds of real Claude Code sessions (450, then 650) on public repos. Stacklit cut tool calls by a quarter to a third but did not lower cost overall. Round 1: pooled cost ratio 1.00 (0.93 to 1.07), cheaper on the largest repo (0.78), more expensive on the two small ones (1.10, 1.23), answers right slightly less often. Round 2, four repos: largest repo 0.89 (0.84 to 0.96), smaller repos 1.05 to 1.61, pooled 1.09 to 1.17, so it cost more on average; answers equally right. See bench/agent-ab/RESULTS.md.
- Not a search engine. When the exact identifier is known, grep is cheaper.

<p align="center"><b>A committed map of your codebase for AI coding agents. 137 tokens for a 19,500 line Go repo.</b></p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://github.com/glincker/stacklit/actions/workflows/ci.yml"><img src="https://github.com/glincker/stacklit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg" alt="CI"></a>
  <a href="https://github.com/glincker/stacklit/releases"><img src="https://badgen.net/github/release/glincker/stacklit" alt="Release"></a>
  <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/stacklit"><img src="https://badgen.net/npm/v/stacklit" alt="npm version"></a>
  <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/stacklit"><img src="https://badgen.net/npm/dm/stacklit" alt="npm downloads"></a>
  <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/glincker/stacklit"><img src="https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/glincker/stacklit.svg" alt="Go reference"></a>
  <a href="LICENSE"><img src="https://badgen.net/badge/license/MIT/green" alt="MIT license"></a>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/assets/demo.gif" alt="stacklit init in a terminal" width="720">
</p>

Stacklit maps your codebase once and keeps the map fresh. It parses your repo with tree-sitter and writes `stacklit.json`: modules, exports, dependency edges and hints. Commit it, and your coding agent reads a few hundred tokens instead of crawling your files, then uses a few commands (`query`, `slice`, `impact`) to go straight to the right file.
Free and MIT, no paid tier. One Go binary, local and deterministic, no LLM, and the CLI makes no network calls. (The map page can load language icons from thesvg.org; `STACKLIT_MAP_ICONS=off` removes that.)

## Install

```bash
npx stacklit init                                   # scan, write the index, open the map
stacklit setup                                      # wire up the assistants it detects
git add stacklit.json && git commit -m "add stacklit index"
```

Also: `brew install glincker/tap/stacklit`, `npm install -g stacklit`, `go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest`, or a binary from [Releases](https://github.com/glincker/stacklit/releases).

## Output

`stacklit derive` prints a compact map for a prompt (gin v1.10.0, 137 tokens, module list trimmed here):

```
gin | go | 8 modules | 19,537 lines | Gin, GitHub Actions, net/http
test: go test ./... | env: PORT

modules:
  binding             binding | depends: bytesconv, json
  internal/bytesconv  bytesconv | depended-by: binding, render, root
  render              render | depends: bytesconv, json
  root                root package | depends: binding, bytesconv, json, render
do-not-touch: .github/
```

`stacklit query` returns a token-budgeted slice of the symbol graph (output trimmed here):

```
$ stacklit query "how is the symbol graph built" --budget 600
internal/cli/graphcmds.go
  50-63 func buildSymbolGraph(root string, includeTests ...bool) (*graph.SymGraph, error)
      calls BuildSymbols E0.95
internal/graph/resolve.go
  955-961 func BuildSymbols(root string, files []string, eo ExtractOptions) *SymGraph
```

## What you get

| | |
|---|---|
| Index | `stacklit.json`, a Mermaid diagram (`DEPENDENCIES.md` by default, set with `output.mermaid`) and an interactive `stacklit.html` map |
| Languages | 48 languages and formats indexed; symbol graph for 20 ([list](docs/LANGUAGES.md)) |
| Queries | `query`, `explain`, `impact`, `path`, `hubs`, `slice`, each with a hard `--budget` |
| MCP | `stacklit serve`: 15 tools, or `--profile minimal` for 4 (about 230 tokens of schema) |
| Hooks | git post-commit refresh; optional Claude Code hook that points a grepped identifier to its definition |
| CI | `export` (graphml, cypher, dot, mermaid and more), `check` architecture rules, `status` freshness, `merge-graphs`, a [GitHub Action](https://github.com/glincker/stacklit-action) |
| Deterministic | same repo, same bytes. A committed index only changes when the code does |
| Privacy | no telemetry, no upload. The map loads language logos from thesvg.org unless `STACKLIT_MAP_ICONS=off` ([details](docs/PRIVACY.md)) |

`stacklit setup` sets up 25 assistants, including Aider, Cline, Continue, OpenCode, Roo Code and Kiro, plus a generic `AGENTS.md` (`stacklit setup --list` shows all 26 targets). Anything else can read `stacklit.json` directly.

Anything else gets line counts and language detection.

## Benchmark

Two tests, with different answers. The first, with no model in the loop: six pinned repos in six languages, 58 tasks, tokens as bytes / 4. The derived map is 137 to 1,351 tokens. On 47 where-is-X questions one `stacklit query` with a 1,000 token budget put the right file first on 81% (95% interval 70 to 91) and in the top five on 96%. Grep with a hand written pattern did better, 89% first and 100% in the top five. The 81% was tuned after looking at failures, so treat it as an upper bound. Method and limits: [bench/RESULTS.md](bench/RESULTS.md).

The second is a real agent test, run twice. Round 1: 450 Claude Code sessions (Sonnet, 30 questions, three public repos, plan written before the first run). Stacklit changed how the agent works but **did not lower cost overall**: pooled cost ratio 1.00 [0.93, 1.07], tokens 1.01 [0.92, 1.10]. It used about a third fewer tool calls (0.68 [0.61, 0.77]), a quarter fewer turns (0.77) and over four fifths fewer grep and glob calls (0.18). Answers were right slightly less often (94.0% to 88.0% on the pre-registered grader, 98.0% to 95.3% audited). Cost ratio by repo (below 1 is cheaper, 50 paired sessions each; full tables, method, limits and the claims we do not make are in [bench/agent-ab/RESULTS.md](bench/agent-ab/RESULTS.md)):

| Repo | Size | Cost ratio [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|
| levelrail | about 16,000 files | 0.78 [0.70, 0.86] |
| theauth-go | about 1,300 files | 1.10 [0.98, 1.25] |
| featuredrop | about 400 files | 1.23 [1.14, 1.33] |

**Round 2** (650 more sessions, 40 new questions, four repos, [bench/agent-ab/RESULTS-round2.md](bench/agent-ab/RESULTS-round2.md)) pointed the same way. The 16,000 file repo was cheaper again (0.89 [0.84, 0.96] with the default wording, 0.87 [0.81, 0.93] with the routed wording). The smaller repos cost more: theauth-go 1.10 and 1.05, featuredrop 1.37 and 1.21, theauth (about 2,900 files) 1.61 and 1.42. Pooled over all four repos a session cost more, not less: 1.17 [1.11, 1.24] and 1.09 [1.04, 1.14]. Tool calls were 0.76 of the no Stacklit count and Grep and Glob calls 0.22 and 0.53. Right answers were equal (97.5%, 97.0%, 97.5%). The model had partly memorised featuredrop, which favours the side without Stacklit. So today Stacklit is for very large repos and "where is it" questions, not for small repos.

**When it helps.** Locate and add-feature questions ("where is it", "where does a new thing go") were 12 to 22 percent cheaper, mostly on the large repo. Trace questions cost the same and were right less often. "Who imports X" cost 1.59x [1.47, 1.72] because one exact grep already answers it. Small repos cost more, since the map is overhead there. The strict setup (crawl guard plus strict rules) measured worse and is off by default.

# Stacklit usage guide

This is the full reference for the `stacklit` command, the MCP server, the configuration file and the `stacklit.json` format. For a short introduction, read the [README](../README.md).

On this page: [Install](#install) | [First run](#first-run) | [Command reference](#command-reference) | [MCP server](#mcp-server) | [Configuration](#configuration) | [Environment variables](#environment-variables) | [Reading stacklit.json](#reading-stacklitjson) | [Monorepos](#monorepo-support) | [Polyrepo scanning](#polyrepo-scanning) | [CI/CD](#cicd) | [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

---

## Install

Pick one:

```bash
npx stacklit init                                              # no install, downloads the binary on first use
npm install -g stacklit                                        # global install
go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest    # from source, needs Go
```

You can also download a binary for macOS, Linux or Windows (amd64 and arm64) from [Releases](https://github.com/glincker/stacklit/releases).

Check the install:

```bash
stacklit --version
```

---

## First run

1. Go to your project.

   ```bash
   cd your-project
   ```

2. Build the index.

   ```bash
   stacklit init
   ```

   The output looks like this:

   ```
   [stacklit] found 342 files
   [stacklit] parsed 342 files (0 errors)
   [stacklit] done in 89ms -- wrote stacklit.json, DEPENDENCIES.md, stacklit.html

   Opening visual map...
   ```

   File counts and timings vary. Go repos index in milliseconds. Python and TypeScript repos can take seconds. See [bench/RESULTS.md](../bench/RESULTS.md) for numbers.

3. Commit the portable outputs. `stacklit.html` is gitignored and comes back with `stacklit view`.

   ```bash
   git add stacklit.json DEPENDENCIES.md
   git commit -m "add stacklit codebase index"
   ```

4. Tell your tools about the index. Run `stacklit setup` to do it for you, or add the lines by hand.

   **Claude Code**, add to `CLAUDE.md`:
   ```
   Read stacklit.json before exploring files. Use modules to locate code, hints for conventions.
   ```

   **Cursor and other MCP clients**, add to the MCP config:
   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "stacklit": { "command": "stacklit", "args": ["serve"] }
     }
   }
   ```

   **Copilot**, add to `.github/copilot-instructions.md`:
   ```
   Read stacklit.json first to understand codebase structure before exploring files.
   ```

   **Any other agent**: `stacklit.json` is plain JSON. Point the agent at it.

---

## Command reference

Every command runs against the current directory. Run `stacklit <command> --help` for the built-in help.

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| [`init`](#stacklit-init) | First scan, write all outputs, open the visual map |
| [`generate`](#stacklit-generate) | Regenerate the outputs from the current source |
| [`view`](#stacklit-view) | Rebuild `stacklit.html` from `stacklit.json` and open it |
| [`diff`](#stacklit-diff) | Check whether the index is stale |
| [`derive`](#stacklit-derive) | Print the compact navigation map, or inject it into an agent config file |
| [`export`](#stacklit-export) | Render the index as markdown, or export the graph as GraphML, Cypher, JSON, DOT, Mermaid, an Obsidian vault or a markdown wiki |
| [`setup`](#stacklit-setup) | Configure detected AI tools and install the git hook |
| [`serve`](#stacklit-serve) | Run the MCP server over stdio |
| [`graph`, `query`, `explain`, `impact`, `path`, `hubs`, `communities`, `report`, `slice`, `watch`](#symbol-graph-commands) | Symbol-level graph and token-budgeted queries |
| [`doctor`](#stacklit-doctor) | Diagnose config, hooks, a stale index and parse errors |
| [`ingest`](#stacklit-ingest) | Add docs, OpenAPI, SQL schemas and ownership to `stacklit.context.json` |
| [`check`](#stacklit-check) | Enforce layer boundaries, cycles, fan-in and fan-out limits and orphans (exit code 3 on violation) |
| [`merge-graphs`](#stacklit-merge-graphs) | Merge symbol graphs from several repos and link them by package names |
| `completion` | Shell completions for bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell |

Global flags: `--version`, `--help`.

### stacklit init

```
stacklit init [--hook] [--summary] [--multi FILE] [--workspace PATH]
```

Scans the current directory, writes `stacklit.json`, `DEPENDENCIES.md` and `stacklit.html`, then opens the HTML in your default browser.

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--hook` | Installs a git `post-commit` hook that runs `stacklit generate --quiet` and stages `stacklit.json` and the configured mermaid file (`DEPENDENCIES.md` by default). An existing hook is appended to, never replaced. |
| `--summary` | Adds an AI-written architecture narrative to the index. See [Summary](#summary-opt-in). |
| `--multi FILE` | Polyrepo mode. Scans every repo path listed in FILE. See [Polyrepo scanning](#polyrepo-scanning). |
| `--workspace PATH` | Accepted, but it has no effect on the scan yet. Monorepo workspaces are detected automatically. |

> [!NOTE]
> The built-in help for `--hook` says "pre-commit". The hook that gets installed is `post-commit`.

> [!NOTE]
> `--summary` is the only opt-in feature that sends data anywhere. Stacklit itself opens no network connection. Whether the command you configure does is up to that command.

### stacklit generate

```
stacklit generate [--quiet]
```

Runs the same scan and writes the same outputs as `init`, without opening a browser. Use it in scripts, hooks and CI.

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--quiet` | Hides progress output |

### stacklit view

```
stacklit view
```

Reads `stacklit.json`, rewrites `stacklit.html` and opens it. It does not rescan your source. Run `generate` first if the code changed.

The HTML is one self-contained file with four views:

- **Graph**: a force-directed dependency map. Click a node to see its exports, types and files.
- **Tree**: a collapsible directory hierarchy with file and line counts.
- **Table**: a sortable module table with search.
- **Flow**: a top-down dependency flow, from entrypoints to leaves.

The Share button downloads a standalone copy.

### stacklit diff

```
stacklit diff
```

Hashes the current source files (a Merkle hash) and compares the result with `merkle_hash` in `stacklit.json`. It prints either "Index is up to date" or a note telling you to run `generate`.

The command exits with status 0 in both cases. A script has to check the output text, or use the GitHub Action's check mode. The command needs an index that has a `merkle_hash` field.

### stacklit derive

```
stacklit derive [--inject claude|cursor|aider]
```

Prints a compact navigation map built from `stacklit.json`. The map has:

- one header line
- an entry and test line
- one line per module, with its purpose and key dependencies
- hot files
- the add-feature hint
- do-not-touch paths

The size grows with the number of modules. A 6-module Go repo gives 122 tokens. A 72-module TypeScript repo gives 1,122. See [bench/RESULTS.md](../bench/RESULTS.md).

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--inject TARGET` | Inserts or replaces the map between marker comments in `CLAUDE.md` (`claude`), `.cursorrules` (`cursor`) or `.aider.conf.yml` (`aider`). The file is created if it is missing. Running it again replaces the previous block. |

### stacklit export

```
stacklit export [--format md] [--source FILE] [-o FILE]
```

Renders the index as markdown for people. Use it for a PR description, an issue or a chat message.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `--format` | `md` | `md`, or a graph format: `graphml`, `cypher`, `json`, `dot`, `mermaid`, `obsidian`, `markdown-wiki` |
| `--scope` | auto | Graph scope for single-file graph formats: `modules` or `symbols`. Auto picks symbols when `stacklit.graph.json` exists. |
| `--graph` | `stacklit.graph.json` | Symbol graph file for graph formats |
| `--budget` | 2000 | Token budget per `markdown-wiki` page. Env: `STACKLIT_EXPORT_PAGE_TOKENS`. |
| `--source` | `stacklit.json` | Index file to read |
| `-o`, `--output` | stdout | Write to this file (one-file formats) or directory (`obsidian`, `markdown-wiki`) instead |

The markdown includes:

- the project title and totals
- a language and framework table
- entrypoints and key directories
- a modules table
- collapsible export lists for each module
- dependency edges, with the most depended on and isolated modules
- hot files, when git data exists
- the hints

The output is deterministic. The same `stacklit.json` always gives byte-identical markdown.

#### Graph formats

Graph formats print to stdout unless you pass `-o`. They never write into the repo on their own. Every node carries `source_file`. Symbol edges carry their confidence (`EXTRACTED`, `INFERRED` or `EXACT`) and a score.

| Format | Output |
|--------|--------|
| `graphml` | One GraphML file (Gephi, yEd, NetworkX) |
| `cypher` | `CREATE` and `MATCH ... CREATE` statements for Neo4j and compatible stores |
| `json` | `{scope, nodes, edges}` |
| `dot` | Graphviz. Inferred edges are dashed. Capped to the highest-degree nodes (`STACKLIT_EXPORT_MAX_NODES`, default 300). |
| `mermaid` | Mermaid flowchart with the same cap |
| `obsidian` | A vault folder. It has `Index.md` plus one note per module, with `[[wikilinks]]` to dependencies. Symbol headings get their own links, as `[[module#Symbol]]`. |
| `markdown-wiki` | `index.md` plus `modules/<module>.md`. Each page is cut off at the token budget with a "... N more" line. The same input gives identical files. |

```
stacklit export --format graphml -o /tmp/graph.graphml
stacklit export --format obsidian -o ~/vault/myproject
stacklit export --format markdown-wiki --budget 1500 -o /tmp/wiki
```

### stacklit setup

```
stacklit setup [claude|cursor|aider]
```

Uses the existing `stacklit.json`, or generates one if none exists. Then it configures your AI tools.

| Target | Detected by | What it changes |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| `claude` | `claude` on PATH, or a `CLAUDE.md` file | Injects the map into `CLAUDE.md`, adds the stacklit server to `.mcp.json` |
| `cursor` | a `.cursor` directory, or `.cursorrules` | Injects the map into `.cursorrules`, adds `.cursor/mcp.json` |
| `aider` | `aider` on PATH, or `.aider.conf.yml` | Injects the map into `.aider.conf.yml` |

With no argument, `setup` configures every tool it detects and installs the post-commit hook. If no tool is detected, it prints the map to stdout so you can paste it yourself.

`.mcp.json` is in this repository's `.gitignore` because it is specific to one user. Decide for your own repo whether to commit it.

#### Claude Code crawl guard

> [!WARNING]
> Not recommended. In the first real-agent A/B, the strict arm (`--crawl-guard=redirect` with steering `d`) cost 1.12x and was right 82.7% of the time. Without Stacklit it was right 94.0% of the time. See [docs/SESSIONS.md](SESSIONS.md#what-the-first-real-agent-ab-measured).

The guard is opt in:

```
stacklit setup claude --crawl-guard[=nudge|redirect|off]
```

It installs a `PreToolUse` hook. The hook spots repo-wide crawls, such as `find .`, `ls -R`, `tree`, `grep -r` or `rg` on the root, `Glob **/*`, a Read of a directory, or a generic "explore the codebase" subagent prompt.

- A bare `--crawl-guard` means `nudge`. Pass a mode after `=` to choose another.
- `nudge` adds a pointer to the stacklit command.
- `redirect` denies the call with a reason that names the command. It does this at most twice in a row per session, and only while the index is current.
- `off` removes the hook. `--uninstall` does the same.

The command supports `--dry-run`. The details are in [docs/SESSIONS.md](SESSIONS.md#crawl-guard).

### stacklit guide

```
stacklit guide [--json]
```

Prints the agent usage guide (rules, command list and examples). You can paste it into any tool.

The rules use the routed wording (steering `e`):

- Use `query` when you do not know where something is.
- Use grep or `impact` when you know the exact name.
- Check the neighbours when the answer is several files.

`STACKLIT_STEERING=d` prints the older strict no-crawl wording. That wording measured worse.

### stacklit refresh, digest and stats

These are session plumbing commands. For the design, see [docs/SESSIONS.md](SESSIONS.md).

```
stacklit refresh --files a.go,b.go [--json]    # or: --stdin with a hook payload
stacklit digest [--check] [--session ID]
stacklit stats [--json] [--since 7d]
```

- `refresh` updates `stacklit.json` (and `stacklit.graph.json` when it exists) for the named files only. Files that have not changed are skipped by content hash. Concurrent callers coalesce behind a lock. Writes are atomic. The result matches a full `generate`.
- `digest` prints the structure hash. It covers module names, edges and exported names only. With `--check`, it exits 0 when the hash matches what the session was given, 1 when it changed, and 2 when nothing was recorded.
- `stats` reports the opt-in local usage log (`STACKLIT_STATS=1`). `served` is measured as bytes/4. `replaced_est` is an estimate of what reading the whole files would have cost. It is not a measured saving.

Claude Code hooks are opt in. They are written to `.claude/settings.json`, or to `~/.claude` with `--global`.

| Flag | Installs |
|---|---|
| `--session-hook` | `SessionStart` for startup, resume, clear and compact. `SubagentStart` for Explore and Plan. |
| `--refresh-hook` | An async `PostToolUse` hook on Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit |

### stacklit serve

```
stacklit serve
```

Starts the MCP server on stdio. Run it from the repo root, because it reads `stacklit.json` from the working directory. See [MCP server](#mcp-server).

### Symbol graph commands

```
stacklit graph                          # build stacklit.graph.json (query commands build it in memory if it is missing)
stacklit query "where is auth checked?" # scoped subgraph for a question, hard limit via --budget (default 2000 tokens)
stacklit explain <symbol>               # definition, location, callers, callees (--budget, default 1500)
stacklit impact <name|file|dir>         # importers of a file or package with file:line, or dependents of a symbol (--depth, --calls)
stacklit path <from> <to>               # shortest path between two symbols
stacklit hubs -n 15                     # most connected symbols
stacklit communities                    # deterministic file clusters with labels
stacklit report -o GRAPH_REPORT.md      # key concepts, surprising links, suggested questions
stacklit slice <symbol>                 # only that symbol's source, with line numbers
stacklit watch                          # keep the graph current as files change
```

**`query`** prints files in relevance order:

- Each file group is numbered (`1. path`). The number comes from the best score among its symbols, with ties broken by path.
- Symbols inside a file are sorted by score, then by line.
- A `best match: <file>:<line> <symbol>` line names the top result.
- The output is byte-stable between runs. When `--budget` cuts results, the lowest ranked ones go first.
- `--order relevance|path` picks the layout. `path` is the older alphabetical grouping, with no numbers. The default comes from `STACKLIT_QUERY_ORDER`, and otherwise it is `relevance`.
- With `--json`, each file has `rank` (1 is best) and `score` (0 to about 1.2, relative to the best seed). Each symbol has its own `score`. Files stay in the printed order.
- The MCP `query_graph` and `query` tools return the same text.

Two scoring knobs:

- `STACKLIT_AUX_PENALTY` (default 0.6) multiplies the score of files under test, example, benchmark or fixture directories. The penalty does not apply when the question names those directories. Set it to 1 to turn it off.
- `STACKLIT_IDENT_TOKEN_BOOST` (default 0.5) raises symbols whose names match a camelCase or snake_case word in the question exactly.

When the question suggests a flow, `query` adds one more line: "several files may take part; also ranked: ...". That line lists the next ranked files, with the `explain` and `path` commands to expand them. It appears in two cases:

- The question contains flow words, such as trace, flow, through, path, calls, wake or lifecycle. `STACKLIT_FLOW_WORDS` replaces that list.
- The top files sit in many different directories with similar scores. The test uses `STACKLIT_QUERY_SPREAD_DIRS` (default 4 of the top `STACKLIT_QUERY_SPREAD_TOP` 5 files, within `STACKLIT_QUERY_FLATNESS` 0.5 of the best score).

The line counts against `--budget`. Single-answer questions do not get it. `STACKLIT_QUERY_NEXT` sets how many files it lists (default 4, at most 5; 0 turns the line off). With `--json`, the files appear in `next`.

**`impact`** answers "who imports X" the way grep would, in fewer tokens. Give it a file path (`src/core.ts`, a unique suffix or a bare name) or a directory (a Go package, such as `internal/appsleep`). It lists the files that import it, one per line as `path:line`. Tests are excluded. The list stays inside `--budget`, with a `[truncated: ...]` line when it is cut.

- A directory means the package in that directory. A subpackage is separate.
- For script languages (TypeScript, JavaScript, Vue, Svelte, Astro), the sources are also read. That catches imports the extractor missed, so the list matches grep. `STACKLIT_IMPACT_SCAN=0` turns this off. `STACKLIT_IMPACT_SCAN_MAX` caps the files read (default 20000).
- An exact symbol name keeps the call-level view, by depth. `--calls` forces that view for files and directories.
- Measured on this repository and three others, the list for a package took about 40 to 160 tokens. `grep -rn` of the same import and the same number of lines took 110 to 390. Before this change, `impact` on a directory returned an error, and on a file it returned a 1,400 token call-level list.

All of these commands accept `--root`, `--graph`, and `--include-tests` (keeps test files in the graph; `STACKLIT_GRAPH_INCLUDE_TESTS=1` does the same). Except for `watch`, they also accept `--json`.

Twenty languages produce symbols and call, import and inheritance edges. The per-language table is in [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md#symbol-graph-extraction).

- `STACKLIT_GRAPH_MAX_PARSE_BYTES` (default 196608) sets the largest file parsed with tree-sitter.
- `STACKLIT_PARSE_MEMORY_MB` bounds the memory used by concurrent parses.
- `watch` uses fsnotify. Above `STACKLIT_WATCH_MAX` directories (default 4096), it falls back to polling. `STACKLIT_WATCH_POLL_MS` sets the polling interval.

### stacklit doctor

```
stacklit doctor [path] [--json] [--strict]
```

Checks the config file, the git hook, index freshness and parse errors. `--strict` also fails on warnings.

### stacklit ingest

```
stacklit ingest [--docs] [--api] [--schema] [--owners] [--git-owners]
```

Writes `stacklit.context.json` next to the index. It leaves `stacklit.json` alone. With no connector flag, every connector runs except `--git-owners`.

Limits: `STACKLIT_INGEST_MAX_BYTES` and `STACKLIT_INGEST_MAX_ITEMS`.

#### Adapters

```
stacklit ingest --adapter "<command>" [--adapter-name NAME] [--adapter-files GLOBS] [--into-graph]
```

An adapter is your own command. Stacklit passes it file paths on stdin, one per line, relative to the root. The command writes JSON Lines back:

- `{"type":"node","id","name","kind","summary","source_file"}`
- `{"type":"edge","from","to","kind"}`

Use adapters for concepts from PDFs, images, audio or anything else Stacklit does not parse. Results go into `stacklit.context.json` as `concepts` and `concept_links`. They are always tagged `INFERRED` and carry a `source` field. A rerun replaces that adapter's earlier output. `--into-graph` also adds them to `stacklit.graph.json` as `concept` nodes.

Stacklit makes no network or model calls itself.

| Variable | Limit |
|----------|-------|
| `STACKLIT_ADAPTER_TIMEOUT_SEC` | 60 seconds |
| `STACKLIT_ADAPTER_MAX_BYTES` | 4 MiB |
| `STACKLIT_ADAPTER_MAX_ITEMS` | 5000 |

The full contract and an example are in [examples/adapters](../examples/adapters/README.md).

#### SCIP

```
stacklit ingest --scip index.scip [--graph stacklit.graph.json]
```

Reads a SCIP index, from `scip-go`, `scip-typescript` or a similar tool, with a built-in decoder. It upgrades `INFERRED` graph edges to `EXACT` where the index shows a reference from the edge's source to a symbol defined at the edge's target. It never adds or removes edges, and it rewrites the graph file in place. The size cap is `STACKLIT_SCIP_MAX_BYTES` (512 MiB).

### stacklit check

```
stacklit check [--root DIR] [--source stacklit.json] [--json]
```

Checks the `check` block of `.stacklitrc.json` against the module graph. It exits with code 3 when a rule is broken and 0 otherwise, so you can use it as a CI step.

```json
{
  "check": {
    "forbidden": [{ "from": "ui/**", "to": "core/db", "reason": "go through the service layer" }],
    "cycles": true,
    "max_fan_in": 12,
    "max_fan_out": 8,
    "orphans": true
  }
}
```

Patterns are module paths with `*` wildcards. `dir/**` matches `dir` and everything below it. With no `check` block, the command passes. `--json` prints `{ok, violations:[{rule, message, modules}]}`.

### stacklit merge-graphs

```
stacklit merge-graphs a/stacklit.graph.json b/stacklit.graph.json -o merged.json [--multi stacklit-multi.json]
```

Combines symbol graphs from several repos. Node IDs get a `repo:` prefix. Each node keeps its `source_file` and gets a `repo` field. To name a repo yourself, use `name=path.json`.

With `--multi`, which takes the output of `generate --multi`, the command adds:

- repo nodes and `depends_on` edges, for repos that depend on each other through manifest package names
- import edges from the importing files to the provider repo

---

## MCP server

```bash
stacklit serve
```

The server exposes fifteen read-only tools. The first seven read `stacklit.json`. The last eight read the symbol graph (`stacklit.graph.json`, built in memory when it is missing).

| Tool | Input | Returns |
|------|-------|---------|
| `get_overview` | none | project name and type, languages, frameworks, entrypoints, file and line totals |
| `get_module` | `name` (exact module name) | one module: purpose, exports, types, dependencies, files, activity |
| `find_module` | `query` (substring) | up to 5 modules whose name or purpose contains the query, case-insensitive. It does not search exports or file names. |
| `list_modules` | none | every module with purpose, file and line counts, activity, sorted by name |
| `get_dependencies` | `module` | the dependency edges that touch that module |
| `get_hot_files` | none | the most changed files in the last 90 days |
| `get_hints` | none | add-feature guidance, test command, env var names, do-not-touch paths |
| `query_graph` | `query`, optional `budget` | scoped symbol subgraph grouped by file, hard token budget (default 2000) |
| `shortest_path` | `from`, `to` | shortest path between two symbols, with the weakest hop's confidence |
| `explain_symbol` | `symbol` | definition, file and line range, signature, callers and callees |
| `impact` | `symbol` (name, `Type.Method`, file path or directory), optional `depth`, `budget` | importers of a file or package with file:line, or the dependents of a symbol |
| `get_hubs` | optional `top` | most connected symbols |
| `get_communities` | none | deterministic file clusters with labels |
| `graph_report` | none | key concepts, surprising links, suggested questions |
| `slice_symbol` | `symbol` | only that symbol's source lines |

The server re-reads `stacklit.json` when its modification time changes. You do not need to restart it after `generate`.

---

## Configuration

Create `.stacklitrc.json` in the project root. The file is optional, and every key in it is optional.

```json
{
  "ignore": ["vendor/", "generated/", "*.pb.go"],
  "max_depth": 3,
  "max_modules": 150,
  "max_exports": 15,
  "output": {
    "json": "stacklit.json",
    "mermaid": "DEPENDENCIES.md",
    "html": "stacklit.html"
  }
}
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `ignore` | none | Extra gitignore-style patterns to skip. They apply on top of `.gitignore` and the built-in skips (`node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `target`, `.venv`, `__pycache__` and similar). |
| `max_depth` | 4 | How deep module detection goes in the directory tree |
| `max_modules` | 200 | Above this many modules, deeper ones collapse into their parents |
| `max_exports` | 10 | Exports kept per module, taken from the files with the most exports first. Symbols past the cap are not in the index. Raise it if lookups by symbol name miss. Env: `STACKLIT_MAX_EXPORTS`. |
| `max_module_files` | 30 | File names listed per module, files with the most exports first. Env: `STACKLIT_MAX_MODULE_FILES`. |
| `module_split_files` | 40 | A module with more files than this is split by subdirectory, repeatedly, so one big directory does not hide its files. Env: `STACKLIT_MODULE_SPLIT_FILES` (`-1` turns splitting off). |
| `output.json`, `output.mermaid`, `output.html` | `stacklit.json`, `DEPENDENCIES.md`, `stacklit.html` | Output file names. The outputs are excluded from the next scan automatically. |
| `timestamps` | false | Writes `generated_at`. Off by default, so a committed index changes only when the code does. Env: `STACKLIT_TIMESTAMPS=1`. |
| `git_activity` | false | Adds git hot and recent files to the index. Off by default for the same reason. Turn it on with this key or with `STACKLIT_GIT=1`. |
| `steering` | `a` | Wording of the rules at the top of the generated `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` block: `a`, `b`, `c`, `d` (strict, measured worse, not recommended) or `e` (routed, not yet measured). See [docs/SESSIONS.md](docs/SESSIONS.md). Env: `STACKLIT_STEERING`. |
| `small_repo_files` | 600 | A repo with fewer indexed source files than this gets a one-line note instead of the digest, in the session hook and in `setup`. 0 turns it off. Env: `STACKLIT_SMALL_REPO_FILES`. |
| `crawl_guard` | (installed mode) | Crawl guard mode: `off`, `nudge` or `redirect`. Env: `STACKLIT_CRAWL_GUARD`. |
| `stats` | false | Appends a local usage log of `query`, `slice`, `explain` and `impact` calls. Env: `STACKLIT_STATS=1`. Never sent over the network. |
| `map_icons` | remote | `remote` lets the HTML map request language logos from thesvg.org when you open it. `off` removes every remote URL and shows letters instead. Env: `STACKLIT_MAP_ICONS=off`. |
| `cache` | true | On-disk parse cache. `STACKLIT_NO_CACHE=1` disables it. |
| `workers` | CPU count | Parser pool size. Env: `STACKLIT_WORKERS`. |
| `parse_memory_mb` | 256 | Soft cap on the estimated memory of concurrent tree-sitter parses. A single file above the cap still parses, alone. Env: `STACKLIT_PARSE_MEMORY_MB` (0 disables the cap). |
| `parse_timeout_ms` | 3000 | Wall-clock budget per file for tree-sitter. A file that goes over is indexed with its line count only, and listed in `scan.lightweight`. Env: `STACKLIT_PARSE_TIMEOUT_MS` (0 disables). |
| `ts_max_bytes` | 131072 | Files larger than this skip tree-sitter (reason `large`). Env: `STACKLIT_TS_MAX_BYTES` (0 disables). |
| `max_line_len` | 2000 | A line longer than this marks the file as minified and skips tree-sitter. Env: `STACKLIT_MAX_LINE_LEN` (0 disables). |
| `skip_generated` | true | Files named `.min.`, `.pb.` or `.gen.`, or marked "generated" or "do not edit" in the first KB, skip tree-sitter. Env: `STACKLIT_SKIP_GENERATED`. |
| `memory_limit_mb` | 448 | Soft Go heap limit during a scan, to keep RSS near the live set. An explicit `GOMEMLIMIT` wins. Env: `STACKLIT_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB` (0 disables). |
| `check` | none | Architecture rules for `stacklit check`: `forbidden`, `cycles`, `max_fan_in`, `max_fan_out`, `orphans` (see [stacklit check](#stacklit-check)) |

Diagnostics:

- `STACKLIT_TRACE=1` prints files whose parse took over 250 ms.
- `STACKLIT_PPROF=<dir>` writes `cpu.pprof`, `heap.pprof` and `heap-peak.pprof`.

A file that is missing, unreadable or invalid JSON is ignored, and the defaults are used.

Only files with recognised source extensions are scanned. Directories named `test`, `tests`, `testdata`, `fixtures`, `e2e`, `bench` or `benchmarks` are left out of the module list. Each module lists up to about 20 file names.

---

## Environment variables

| Variable | Used by | Meaning |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `STACKLIT_SUMMARY_CMD` | `init --summary` | Command (split on whitespace) that reads a prompt on stdin and prints the summary. Default: `claude -p`. |
| `STACKLIT_SUMMARY_TIMEOUT` | `init --summary` | Timeout in seconds. Default: 120. |
| `STACKLIT_EXPORT_PAGE_TOKENS` | `export --format markdown-wiki`, `obsidian` | Token budget per page. Default: 2000. |
| `STACKLIT_EXPORT_MAX_NODES` | `export --format dot`, `mermaid` | Node cap, highest degree kept. Default: 300. |
| `STACKLIT_ADAPTER_TIMEOUT_SEC`, `STACKLIT_ADAPTER_MAX_BYTES`, `STACKLIT_ADAPTER_MAX_ITEMS` | `ingest --adapter` | Adapter timeout, output size and item caps. Defaults: 60, 4194304, 5000. |
| `STACKLIT_DIGEST_TOKENS` | `setup`, hooks | Token cap of the injected digest. Default 500. |
| `STACKLIT_STEERING` | `setup`, `guide`, `serve` | Steering wording variant `a`, `b`, `c`, `d` or `e`. `d` also selects the older MCP and guide wording. |
| `STACKLIT_SMALL_REPO_FILES` | `setup`, hooks | Source file count below which a repo gets the small repo note instead of the digest. Default 600, 0 off. |
| `STACKLIT_QUERY_NEXT`, `STACKLIT_FLOW_WORDS`, `STACKLIT_QUERY_SPREAD_DIRS`, `STACKLIT_QUERY_SPREAD_TOP`, `STACKLIT_QUERY_FLATNESS` | `query` | The "also ranked" line: files listed (default 4, 0 off), flow word list, and the spread test (defaults 4, 5, 0.5). |
| `STACKLIT_IMPACT_SCAN`, `STACKLIT_IMPACT_SCAN_MAX` | `impact` | `0` stops `impact` from reading script sources to confirm importers. The cap sets how many files are read (default 20000). |
| `STACKLIT_CRAWL_GUARD` | `hook crawl` | `off`, `nudge` or `redirect`. Overrides the `crawl_guard` config key and the mode the hook was installed with. Off by default when nothing sets it. |
| `STACKLIT_CRAWL_REDIRECTS`, `STACKLIT_CRAWL_FRESH_TTL` | `hook crawl` | Consecutive redirects per session before the guard stands down (default 2). Seconds a staleness verdict is reused (default 10). |
| `STACKLIT_CRAWL_MAX_DEPTH`, `STACKLIT_CRAWL_PROMPT_CHARS` | `hook crawl` | Deepest `find -maxdepth` or `tree -L` still treated as narrow (default 1). Longest subagent prompt judged generic (default 600). |
| `STACKLIT_CRAWL_POINTER_MAX_BYTES`, `STACKLIT_CRAWL_STATE_DAYS` | `hook crawl` | Largest graph loaded to build an exact pointer (default 8 MiB). Days before session state files are pruned (default 7). |
| `STACKLIT_STATS` | `query`, `slice`, `explain`, `impact` | `1` logs usage locally. `0` forces logging off. |
| `STACKLIT_CACHE_DIR` | cache, hooks, stats | Where the parse cache, session state and usage log live. |
| `STACKLIT_REFRESH_DEBOUNCE_MS`, `STACKLIT_LOCK_STALE_SEC` | `refresh` | Debounce before a refresh (default 30). Age at which a lock counts as abandoned (default 30). |
| `STACKLIT_SUBAGENT_TYPES` | `hook subagent` | Comma-separated list of agent types that get the digest. Default `Explore,Plan`. |
| `STACKLIT_SCIP_MAX_BYTES` | `ingest --scip` | Largest SCIP file read. Default: 512 MiB. |

### Summary (opt-in)

`stacklit init --summary` runs the command above with a prompt. The prompt has a short instruction and a JSON snapshot of the index: project, tech, modules with exports and dependencies, and entrypoints. No file contents are included.

The output is stored under `architecture.ai_summary` in `stacklit.json`. If the command fails, Stacklit prints a warning and writes the index without a summary.

---

## Reading stacklit.json

### Project and tech

```json
{
  "project": { "name": "my-app", "type": "monorepo" },
  "tech": {
    "primary_language": "typescript",
    "languages": { "typescript": { "files": 120, "lines": 14000 } },
    "frameworks": ["React", "Express"]
  },
  "structure": {
    "entrypoints": ["src/index.ts"],
    "total_files": 120,
    "total_lines": 14000
  }
}
```

`tech.framework_patterns` adds detected routes, API, middleware and entry locations for known frameworks. `merkle_hash` is the content hash that `stacklit diff` and the git hook use to skip regeneration that is not needed.

### Modules

Each module is a directory of related source files:

```json
"src/auth": {
  "purpose": "Authentication and authorization",
  "language": "typescript",
  "files": 8,
  "lines": 1200,
  "file_list": ["service.ts", "middleware.ts", "types.ts"],
  "exports": ["AuthProvider", "useSession()", "loginAction(email, password)"],
  "type_defs": { "AuthState": "user User, token string, isLoading boolean" },
  "depends_on": ["src/db", "src/config"],
  "depended_by": ["src/api", "src/middleware"],
  "activity": "high"
}
```

- **purpose** comes from the directory name and a built-in vocabulary. It is generic. For example, a `json` directory gets "Json". It is not a semantic summary.
- **exports** are public functions, classes and types, with signatures where the language provides them. The count is capped by `max_exports`.
- **type_defs** are field definitions of key structs, interfaces and classes.
- **depends_on** and **depended_by** come from the module graph, which is built from import statements. Entries are sometimes shortened to the last path segment.
- **activity** is `high`, `medium` or `low`, based on git commit frequency over 90 days.

### Dependencies

```json
"dependencies": {
  "edges": [["src/api", "src/auth"], ["src/auth", "src/db"]],
  "most_depended": ["src/db", "src/config"],
  "isolated": ["scripts"]
}
```

`most_depended` ranks modules by number of dependents. `isolated` lists modules with no edges in or out.

### Git and hints

```json
"git": { "hot_files": [{ "path": "src/api/routes.ts", "commits_90d": 14 }] },
"hints": {
  "add_feature": "Add handler in src/api, register in src/index.ts",
  "test_command": "npm test",
  "env_vars": ["DATABASE_URL", "JWT_SECRET"],
  "do_not_touch": ["migrations/", ".github/"]
}
```

`env_vars` lists names found in `os.Getenv`, `process.env` and `os.environ` style accesses. Stacklit never reads the values. Hints are heuristics. The test command comes from well-known build files. The add-feature hint comes from module names such as `api` or `handler`.

---

## Monorepo support

Workspaces are detected automatically. They show up as module groups in the index.

| Tool | Detection |
|------|-----------|
| pnpm | `pnpm-workspace.yaml` |
| npm, yarn | `package.json` `workspaces` field |
| Go | `go.work` |
| Turborepo | `turbo.json` |
| Nx | `nx.json` |
| Lerna | `lerna.json` |
| Cargo | `Cargo.toml` `[workspace]` section |
| Convention | `apps/`, `packages/`, `services/`, `libs/` directories |

---

## Polyrepo scanning

Scan several separate repositories at once.

1. Write one repo path per line into a file.

   ```bash
   echo "/path/to/repo-a" > repos.txt
   echo "/path/to/repo-b" >> repos.txt
   ```

2. Run the scan with that file.

   ```bash
   stacklit init --multi repos.txt
   ```

Blank lines and `#` comments in the file are skipped. The result is `stacklit-multi.json` in the current directory. It holds module data for each repo and combined totals. Cross-repo dependency edges are not computed yet. That is on the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md).

---

## CI/CD

### GitHub Action

[glincker/stacklit-action](https://github.com/glincker/stacklit-action) keeps the index fresh:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: glincker/stacklit-action@v1            # auto-commit (default)
# or: with: { mode: check }                   # fail the PR if the index is stale
```

In auto-commit mode, give the job `permissions: contents: write`.

### Hand-written workflow

```yaml
name: Update stacklit index
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore: ['stacklit.json', 'DEPENDENCIES.md', '**.md']

jobs:
  stacklit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.25'
      - run: go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest
      - run: stacklit generate --quiet
      - uses: stefanzweifel/git-auto-commit-action@v5
        with:
          commit_message: "chore: update stacklit index"
          file_pattern: "stacklit.json DEPENDENCIES.md"
```

### Git hook

```bash
stacklit init --hook     # or: stacklit setup
```

The hook runs `stacklit generate --quiet` after each commit. It stages the two committed outputs for the next commit.

---

## Troubleshooting

**The session hook does not fire, the index looks stale, or two sessions collide.** See the troubleshooting section of [docs/SESSIONS.md](docs/SESSIONS.md). Quick checks:

- `/hooks` in Claude Code
- `echo '{"source":"startup","cwd":"'$PWD'"}' | stacklit hook session`
- `stacklit status`
- `stacklit refresh --files <paths>`

**`could not read stacklit.json`.** Run `stacklit init` or `stacklit generate` first, and run the command from the repo root.

**A symbol is missing from the index.** Exports are capped per module. Raise `max_exports` in `.stacklitrc.json`, then regenerate. Unexported (private) symbols are never listed.

**A dependency looks wrong.** The graph comes from import statements resolved to modules. Test files and relative imports can add or drop edges. Confirm with a read, and open an issue with a minimal example.

**Generation is slow or uses a lot of memory on Python or TypeScript.** This is a known cost of the pure-Go tree-sitter parsers. Add large generated or vendored directories to `ignore`.

**Windows install problems.** Use `go install`, or download the binary from Releases and put it on your PATH.

---

Next: [How it works](ARCHITECTURE.md), or the [FAQ](FAQ.md) if something looks off.


---

<!-- source: docs/INSTALL.md -->

# Install

Every way to get Stacklit, with the exact command. The status column says whether a path works today. Paths marked "after" are not live yet, and the column says what they wait for.

## Quick pick

| Path | Command | Gives you | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| npx | `npx stacklit init` | CLI, one run, no install | live |
| npm global | `npm install -g stacklit` | CLI | live |
| Homebrew | `brew install glincker/tap/stacklit` | CLI | live |
| go install | `go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest` | CLI | live |
| install.sh | see below | CLI, checksum verified | live once this file is on the default branch |
| Release archive | download from GitHub Releases | CLI | live |
| Docker | `docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work ghcr.io/glincker/stacklit init` | CLI in a container | after the image is published (see below) |
| Claude Code plugin | two commands below | hooks, skill and MCP server | live once this file is on the default branch |
| MCP registry | `io.github.glincker/stacklit` | MCP server entry for registry-aware clients | after the next npm release and a registry publish |
| skills.sh | `npx skills add glincker/stacklit` | the skill only | should work from the GitHub repo. Listing on skills.sh is unverified. |

What each path gives you:

| | CLI | Hooks | Skill | MCP server |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| npx, npm, brew, go install, install.sh, archive, Docker | yes | via `stacklit setup` | via `stacklit setup` | via `stacklit setup` |
| Claude Code plugin | needs the CLI on PATH | yes | yes | yes (minimal profile) |
| MCP registry | needs npm or the CLI | no | no | yes |
| skills.sh | no | no | yes | no |

## Command line

```bash
npx stacklit init                 # no install
npm install -g stacklit
brew install glincker/tap/stacklit
go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest
```

Then, in your repo:

```bash
stacklit init
```

## install.sh

The script detects your OS and architecture (Linux and macOS, amd64 and arm64). It downloads the release archive and `checksums.txt`, checks the sha256, and installs to `~/.local/bin`. It does not need sudo.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/stacklit/master/scripts/install.sh | sh
```

Put options after `sh -s --`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/stacklit/master/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --version 0.5.0 --prefix /usr/local
```

- `--dry-run` downloads and verifies the archive, but installs nothing.
- To read the script first, open `scripts/install.sh`. It is short.
- The script does not support Windows. Use npm, or the zip from Releases.

## Docker

The repository has a multi-stage `docker/Dockerfile`. The final image is distroless, and its entrypoint is `stacklit`. Build it yourself:

```bash
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile --build-arg VERSION=0.5.0 -t stacklit .
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work stacklit init
```

Once the image is published to ghcr.io, you can skip the build:

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work ghcr.io/glincker/stacklit init
```

On Linux, add `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"` so the generated files belong to you.

> [!WARNING]
> The image has no shell and no git binary. Features that call git do not work in it: hot files, and the post-commit hook installer. Use the native binary for those. The MCP server works over Docker for the index tools: `docker run -i --rm -v "$PWD":/work ghcr.io/glincker/stacklit serve`.

## Claude Code plugin

The repo is a Claude Code plugin marketplace. The plugin needs the `stacklit` binary on your PATH. Any CLI path above works.

1. Add the marketplace.

   ```bash
   claude plugin marketplace add glincker/stacklit
   ```

2. Install the plugin.

   ```bash
   claude plugin install stacklit@stacklit
   ```

Inside a session, the same two steps are `/plugin marketplace add glincker/stacklit` and `/plugin install stacklit@stacklit`.

The plugin adds:

- the Stacklit skill
- a SessionStart hook (`stacklit hook session`) that injects the map
- an async PostToolUse hook (`stacklit hook posttool`) that refreshes the map for edited files
- an MCP server that runs `stacklit serve --profile minimal`

Both hooks exit quietly if `stacklit` is not installed. The crawl guard is not included. Turn it on with `stacklit setup claude --crawl-guard`. The hook wrapper uses `sh`, so on Windows it needs Git Bash.

## MCP registry

`server.json` at the repo root describes the server for the official MCP registry, under the name `io.github.glincker/stacklit`. It points at the npm package, which declares the same name in `mcpName`.

That field ships with the first npm release after it was added. The maintainers publish the registry entry after that release. Until then, use `stacklit setup` or the plugin to wire up the MCP server.

## Skill only

```bash
npx skills add glincker/stacklit
```

This installs `skills/stacklit/SKILL.md` into the agents it detects. The skill follows the open Agent Skills format.

## Not available yet

Scoop, WinGet, Nix, AUR, mise and a devcontainer feature are not published. Windows users can use `npm install -g stacklit` or the zip from Releases.

Next: [Quickstart](USAGE.md#first-run), or the full [usage guide](USAGE.md).


---

| <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/glincker/thesvg@main/public/icons/powershell/default.svg" alt="PowerShell" width="24" height="24"> | PowerShell | Import-Module/using/dot-sourcing, functions with params, classes |
| <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/glincker/thesvg@main/public/icons/gleam/default.svg" alt="Gleam" width="24" height="24"> | Gleam | imports, pub functions, types with constructors, constants |
| <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/glincker/thesvg@main/public/icons/cmake/default.svg" alt="CMake" width="24" height="24"> | CMake | include/add_subdirectory/find_package, project, library/executable/custom targets, functions, macros |
|  | Makefile | includes, explicit targets with prerequisites |
| <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/glincker/thesvg@main/public/icons/docker/default.svg" alt="Dockerfile" width="24" height="24"> | Dockerfile | base images, build stages, exposed ports |
| <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/glincker/thesvg@main/public/icons/yaml/default.svg" alt="YAML / TOML / JSON" width="24" height="24"><img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/glincker/thesvg@main/public/icons/toml/default.svg" alt="YAML / TOML / JSON" width="24" height="24"><img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/glincker/thesvg@main/public/icons/json/default.svg" alt="YAML / TOML / JSON" width="24" height="24"> | YAML / TOML / JSON | top-level keys (capped, see below) |
| <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/glincker/thesvg@main/public/icons/graphql/default.svg" alt="GraphQL" width="24" height="24"> | GraphQL | object/interface/enum/input/union/scalar types with fields, named operations and fragments |

## Limits and parser notes

- **Config files** (YAML, TOML, JSON) report at most `STACKLIT_CONFIG_KEY_CAP` top-level keys (default 40). Files above `STACKLIT_CONFIG_MAX_BYTES` (default 262144) skip key extraction.
- **Skipped files**: lockfiles and the generated `stacklit.json` are not indexed.
- **Parsers**: Go uses the Go standard library. Every other row uses tree-sitter.
- **SQL**: `$$` function bodies are masked before parsing, so the statements after them still extract.
- **Groovy** falls back to line patterns where the grammar fails.
- **`.m` files** are treated as Objective-C.

## Symbol graph

The symbol graph (`stacklit graph`, `query`, `impact`, `slice`) covers 20 languages. The per-language table is in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md#symbol-graph-extraction). The other languages still get the module index.

## Monorepos

Monorepos are detected automatically:

- pnpm, npm and yarn workspaces
- Go workspaces
- Turborepo, Nx and Lerna
- Cargo workspaces
- `apps/`, `packages/`, `services/` and `libs/` directories


---

<!-- source: docs/FAQ.md -->

# FAQ

Short answers on what Stacklit reads, when it helps, how accurate its dependency edges are, and how it fits with git and AI assistants.

## Does it read my code?

Yes, locally. It uses tree-sitter to extract structure. Nothing leaves your machine unless you pass `--summary`. See [Privacy](PRIVACY.md).

## Does it help on small repos?

Less. If the whole repo fits in a prompt, an agent can just read it.

The index pays off once exploring costs more than reading a map. That happens when an agent would otherwise open several large files just to confirm where something lives.

## When is grep better?

When you already know the exact identifier. One grep is cheaper than loading a map.

The index helps with questions grep cannot answer in one step, such as "what depends on this module" or "where would a new adapter go".

## How accurate are the dependency edges?

Module-level edges come from import statements. They are good enough to orient an agent, but they are not exact.

In the benchmark, 4 of 7 "what depends on X" lookups were fully correct. Known weak spots:

- Test files counted as dependents.
- Relative imports resolved to the wrong module.
- Short module names that can be ambiguous.

Treat the graph as a guide, and confirm with a read.

## What if my language is not supported?

Stacklit still counts the files and detects their language. The module map, git activity and hints still work. Exports and dependency edges need a parser.

## Does the git hook slow commits down?

The hook runs `stacklit generate --quiet` after each commit.

- On Go repos of this size, it takes tens of milliseconds.
- On Python and TypeScript repos in the benchmark, it took a few seconds.

If that is too slow, run `stacklit generate` by hand, or run it in CI instead.

## Can I keep the Mermaid file out of the repo root?

Yes. Set `"output": {"mermaid": "docs/DEPENDENCIES.md"}` in `.stacklitrc.json`. The git hook stages the configured path.

## Can I use it with Copilot?

Yes. Commit `stacklit.json`, then tell Copilot to read it in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. You can also paste the output of `stacklit derive` there.

## How is it different from dumping the whole repo into a prompt?

A dump is the full source. Stacklit is structure only. It is orders of magnitude smaller, but it cannot answer questions that need code bodies.

For a factual feature comparison, see [COMPARISON.md](COMPARISON.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/PRIVACY.md -->

# Privacy

Stacklit runs on your machine. It reads your source files, writes its outputs into your repository, and makes no network requests of its own.

## What it does not do

- No telemetry, no analytics, no account and no upload.
- The program makes no network requests of its own. The two exceptions are below: the HTML map and `--summary`.
- Network activity during install is separate. `npx stacklit` and `npm install -g stacklit` download the release binary from GitHub.

## The HTML map

The map is one file. It has no scripts or fonts from other hosts. The only thing it fetches is small language logos.

When you open the map, it requests one icon file per language and framework. For example, `https://thesvg.org/icons/go/default.svg`. A copy of each icon is on cdn.jsdelivr.net as a backup.

- The requests carry only the icon name. They send no repo data, no cookies and no referrer.
- A Content-Security-Policy blocks every other request.
- The page works offline. It shows letters where the logos would be.
- To leave no remote URL in the page, set `STACKLIT_MAP_ICONS=off`, or `"map_icons": "off"` in `.stacklitrc.json`.

## The one opt-in exception

`stacklit init --summary` is the only feature that sends data to another program. It pipes a snapshot of the index to a command you control. The snapshot has module names, exports, dependency edges and entrypoints. It has no file contents.

The command is `claude -p` by default. You can change it with `STACKLIT_SUMMARY_CMD`. Whether that command talks to a network is up to that command. Without the flag, nothing is sent anywhere.

## What is in `stacklit.json`

The index lists the names of modules, files and exported symbols. It also lists detected environment variable names, but never their values.

If your repo is private, review the index before you commit it to a public place.


---

<!-- source: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md -->

# Architecture

Stacklit is one Go binary. It walks a repository, parses each source file into a small record of imports and exports, groups files into modules, resolves imports into module-level edges, and writes the result in several formats.

The core path has no daemon, no database and no network client.

## Pipeline

`stacklit generate` (and `init`) run one pipeline, implemented in `internal/engine/engine.go`:

```
walk files -> parse each file -> build module graph -> git activity -> assemble index -> render outputs
```

| Step | Package | What it does |
|------|---------|--------------|
| Config | `internal/config` | Loads an optional `.stacklitrc.json` over the defaults (depth, module and export caps, ignore patterns, output names) |
| Monorepo detection | `internal/monorepo` | Detects pnpm, npm and yarn workspaces, `go.work`, Turborepo, Nx, Lerna, Cargo workspaces and convention directories |
| Walk | `internal/walker` | Lists indexable source files in sorted order. Honors `.gitignore`, config ignores and built-in skips (`node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `target`, virtualenvs). Keeps only known source extensions. |
| Parse | `internal/parser` | Turns each file into a `FileInfo`: language, imports, exports with signatures, type definitions, line count and an entrypoint flag |
| Graph | `internal/graph` | Groups files into modules by directory, resolves imports to modules, and produces edges, most-depended and isolated lists |
| Detect | `internal/detect` | Frameworks (from imports and config files), framework patterns (routes, API, middleware, entry), and environment variable names |
| Git | `internal/git` | 90-day commit counts per file (hot files), recent files, the Merkle content hash, and the post-commit hook installer |
| Assemble | `internal/engine` | Builds the `schema.Index`, derives purpose strings and hints (add feature, test command, do-not-touch) |
| Summary (optional) | `internal/summary` | With `--summary`, runs a user-configured command on an index snapshot |
| Render | `internal/renderer` | Writes `stacklit.json`, `DEPENDENCIES.md` (Mermaid), `stacklit.html` and the markdown export |

Other consumers of the index:

| Package | Role |
|---------|------|
| `internal/derive` | Builds the compact navigation map and injects it between marker comments in agent config files |
| `internal/setup` | Detects Claude Code, Cursor and Aider, and writes their config and MCP entries |
| `internal/mcp` | MCP server over stdio, backed by `stacklit.json` |
| `internal/cli` | Cobra commands that wire the above together |
| `internal/schema` | The `Index` types shared by every package |

## Parsers

`internal/parser/parser.go` keeps an ordered registry. For each file, it uses the first parser whose `CanParse` accepts the file.

1. **`GoParser`** uses the standard library `go/parser`. It gives exact signatures and struct fields, with no external dependency.
2. **`TreeSitterParser`** handles TypeScript, JavaScript, TSX, JSX, Python, Rust, Java, C#, Ruby, PHP, Kotlin, Swift, C and C++. It uses a pure-Go tree-sitter runtime (no cgo). The binary therefore cross-compiles to every release target without a C toolchain. Each language has an extractor in `internal/parser/ts_*.go`.
3. **`GenericParser`** is the fallback. It records only the line count and language.

To add a language, write an extractor and register it in `tsLangMap`. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Modules and dependency resolution

A module is a directory.

- A file belongs to its parent directory, cut to at most `max_depth` path segments.
- Files at the repo root belong to `root`.
- Modules with a path segment named `test`, `tests`, `__tests__`, `testdata`, `fixtures`, `e2e`, `benchmarks`, `bench` or `docs_src` are left out of the graph.
- When the module count would go over `max_modules`, deeper modules fold into their parents.

Edges come from import statements:

- Each import string is matched against the known module names. The longest match wins.
- Relative imports resolve against the importing file's directory.
- Python dot-style imports are normalized first.
- Go imports match on the module path.
- Anything that matches no module is treated as external and dropped.

This is deliberately approximate. It works from import text, not from a type-checked symbol graph. It can miss dynamic imports and re-exports, and it can add edges that come from test files. [bench/RESULTS.md](../bench/RESULTS.md) measures how often the "what depends on X" answers are exactly right.

## The index

`internal/schema` defines `stacklit.json`. Its top-level sections are `project`, `tech`, `structure`, `modules`, `dependencies`, `git`, `hints`, `architecture` and `merkle_hash`. For a field-by-field description, see [USAGE.md](USAGE.md#reading-stacklitjson).

Determinism is a design goal. Files are walked in sorted order, maps are written with stable key order, and paths are normalized to forward slashes. The same source tree should give the same index on any OS. That is what makes the index safe to commit and to diff.

## Symbol graph extraction

`internal/graph` turns source files into symbols (functions, methods and types) and edges between them.

- Go uses the standard library AST.
- Every other language goes through one shared tree-sitter driver, `ts_driver.go`. The driver walks the parse tree once. A small table per language sets the details: which node types define symbols, which are calls, and how imports and base types are read. The tables live in `ts_lang_core.go` and `ts_lang_more.go`.
- Each symbol carries its start and end line, a one-line signature, the first sentence of its doc comment, and its visibility.

### Memory limits

- Concurrent parses share a weighted gate, sized by `STACKLIT_PARSE_MEMORY_MB` (default 512).
- A file larger than `STACKLIT_GRAPH_MAX_PARSE_BYTES` (default 192 KiB) skips tree-sitter.
- Python, TypeScript and JavaScript, Rust and Java fall back to the older line scanner in that case. Other languages keep only their file node.
- The line scanner also takes over when a Python tree disagrees with the file's indentation. The grammar runtime can drop a block without an error.
- Test files are skipped unless you pass `--include-tests` or set `STACKLIT_GRAPH_INCLUDE_TESTS=1`.

### Edge kinds by language

- **def**: the symbol has a span, a signature, a doc comment and a visibility.
- **typed**: receiver types are inferred from annotated parameters, typed locals, typed fields or constructor assignments. So `repo.find()` links to `Repo.find`, not to every `find`.

| Language | def | calls | imports | inherits | implements | typed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Go | yes | yes | yes | embedding | structural (inferred) | yes |
| Python | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | yes |
| TypeScript, JavaScript | yes | yes | yes (import, require, re-export) | yes | yes (TypeScript) | yes |
| Rust | yes | yes | yes (use, mod) | trait bounds | impl Trait for | yes |
| Java | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| C# | yes | yes | yes (using) | yes | by position and I-prefix | yes |
| Kotlin | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Swift | yes | yes | module imports | yes | by position | yes |
| PHP | yes | yes | yes (use) | yes | yes | yes |
| Ruby | yes | yes | yes (require, require_relative) | yes | include, extend | yes |
| C | yes | yes | yes (#include, header and source pair) | no | no | yes |
| C++ | yes | yes | yes (#include) | yes | no | yes |
| Scala | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Dart | yes | yes | yes | yes | with, implements | yes |
| Elixir | yes | yes | yes (alias, import, use, require) | no | no | no |
| Lua | yes | yes | yes (require) | no | no | no |
| Zig | yes | yes | yes (@import) | no | no | no |
| Haskell | yes | yes | yes | no | no | no |
| OCaml | yes | yes | yes (open, qualified paths) | no | no | no |
| Solidity | yes | yes | yes | yes | by I-prefix | yes |

When a clause lists bases without saying which are classes (C#, Swift, Scala, Solidity), the first non-interface name counts as `inherits`. The rest, and any name shaped like `IName`, count as `implements`.

### Call resolution and confidence

Resolution is one pass over hash maps that are built once. So the cost grows linearly with the number of references.

A call is resolved in this order. The first rule that matches wins.

1. The same file, including the enclosing type's own methods.
2. Names imported from a file in the repo, then the package or namespace of the file.
3. Wildcard and namespace imports, in sorted order, so the output is stable.
4. A typed receiver (`@Type`), then that type's ancestors. For `this`, `self` and `super`, the enclosing type and its ancestors.
5. A qualifier bound to an import (`mod.fn`, `Alias.method`).
6. A last resort: a name guess across the repo.

A receiver whose type is known but lives outside the repo (`String`, or a library class) links to nothing. It does not link to a project method with the same name.

| Score | Confidence | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.00 | EXTRACTED | Same-file definition, or a unique type in the same file |
| 0.95 | EXTRACTED | Imported name that resolves to one definition |
| 0.90 | EXTRACTED | Qualified through an import, a wildcard import, a typed receiver or `this` |
| 0.85 | EXTRACTED | Static call on a project type |
| 0.80 | EXTRACTED | Method found on an ancestor type, or a member of a bound module whose owner name differs |
| 0.60 | INFERRED | Base type found only by unique name |
| 0.55 | INFERRED | Unknown receiver, one method of that name in the repo |
| 0.50 | INFERRED | Unqualified name, one function of that name in the repo |
| 0.45 | INFERRED | Receiver type is in the repo, but no method was found on it |
| 0.25 to 0.50 | INFERRED | Several candidates (at most four). The score is split by candidate count. |
| 0.30 | INFERRED | Generic names such as `get` or `close` with an unknown receiver |

Prototype-only declarations (C and C++ headers) are dropped as call targets when a definition with the same name is also a candidate.

## Staleness detection

`ComputeMerkle` hashes the sorted list of source files and their contents into one root hash. The hash is stored as `merkle_hash`. `stacklit diff` recomputes it and compares.

The hash covers only indexed source files. Edits to docs or config files do not make the index look stale.

## Compact map and injection

`derive.CompactMap` prints one line per module. The line holds the purpose, up to four dependencies, and up to four dependents when there are three or more. The map also has a header, hot files and hints.

`InjectIntoFile` wraps the map in start and end marker comments. Re-runs replace the block in place, so agent config files stay clean across regenerations. The map grows with the module count, which is why `max_modules` also bounds its size.

## MCP server

`internal/mcp` registers fifteen read-only tools with the official Go MCP SDK. Seven read the index and eight read the symbol graph. It serves them over stdio. Each call loads `stacklit.json` from the working directory and caches it until the file's modification time changes.

## Network use

The core path makes no network calls.

- `internal/summary` runs a local command only when you pass `--summary`. The command is `claude -p` by default, or whatever `STACKLIT_SUMMARY_CMD` names.
- The repository also has `internal/summary/ai.go`, a direct API client. No command calls it today.
- The HTML output embeds everything it needs and loads nothing remotely.
- The npm wrapper downloads the release binary from GitHub when you install.

## Release and CI

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `go vet`, `go test -race`, and a build on Linux, macOS and Windows.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` with `.goreleaser.yml`: cross-compiled binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows on amd64 and arm64, plus an npm publish with trusted publishing.
- `.github/workflows/stacklit-index.yml`: regenerates this repository's own index on pushes to the default branch.
- `action/action.yml`: a composite action that installs stacklit and runs `generate`.
- `npm/`: the `npx stacklit` wrapper that downloads the matching release binary.

## Benchmarks

`bench/` is a separate `package main` inside the same module. It runs the built `stacklit` binary and reads `stacklit.json` as generic JSON. It does not import the internal packages, so it cannot change the shipped binary.

<!-- source: skills/stacklit/SKILL.md -->

---
name: stacklit
description: Use the stacklit codebase map (stacklit.json) to locate code and check blast radius before grep or glob.
---

Read `stacklit.json` before broad searches.

1. Missing or stale: `stacklit generate`.
2. Find the module by `purpose`, then read only its `file_list`.
3. Before editing, check `depended_by` and `dependencies.most_depended`.
4. New code goes where `hints.add_feature` says; verify with `hints.test_command`.
5. Respect `hints.do_not_touch`.

MCP tools, if connected: `get_overview`, `find_module`, `get_module`, `get_dependencies`, `list_modules`, `get_hot_files`, `get_hints`.

Docs, APIs, schemas, owners: `stacklit ingest`, then read `stacklit.context.json`.
Index drift: `stacklit diff`.
